title: Initial VVA project setup
summary: This commit establishes the foundational structure for the VVA (Version & Workflow Automator) project. It adds a comprehensive set of source files, configuration files, and dependencies required to run the application locally and to orchestrate the Git‑to‑AI‑to‑Document pipeline.
purposeAndRationale: The purpose of this commit is to bootstrap the VVA codebase, providing the core CLI, React UI, Git data collection logic, AI analysis engine, and document generation utilities. It also includes environment configuration, package manifests, and lock files to ensure reproducible builds.
technicalChanges: Added environment example with NVIDIA API key and model configuration
Created .gitignore to exclude build artifacts and logs
Provided README with local run instructions
Implemented ai/ai_engine.py to invoke NVIDIA API for commit analysis
Added ai/test_nvidia.py for API connectivity test
Created bin/vva.js as CLI entry point
Generated bun.lock with full dependency tree
Set up index.html and metadata.json for web deployment
Included comprehensive project description in public/assets
Defined JSON schemas for AI response and project data
Built React application entry point (src/App.tsx) and main.tsx
Implemented CLI command modules (init, report, status, watch)
Implemented core Git utilities for repository detection and data extraction
Implemented core collector for gathering commit metadata and diffs
Implemented core Python module for invoking AI and document engines
Created UI components for terminal, collector, AI engine, document generation, architecture, team, and header
Added utility functions for orchestrating data flow and generating structured AI responses
Added TypeScript types for VVA data structures
Added PDF and Word export utilities
Configured TypeScript compiler options and Vite build settings
architecturalImpact: The commit establishes a layered architecture: a Node.js orchestrator (CLI & React UI) coordinates Git data collection, AI analysis, and document generation. The AI engine runs in Python, communicating via JSON files. The project is modularized into commands, core utilities, components, and schemas, enabling clear separation of concerns and facilitating future extensions.
observationsAndLimitations: The commit only adds files; no functional tests or CI configuration are present.
The AI engine script relies on an NVIDIA API key hard‑coded in .env.example, which may not be secure for production.
The bun.lock file is extremely large, potentially impacting install times.
The project includes both Node.js and Python components but does not provide a unified build or deployment pipeline.
No error handling for missing dependencies or environment variables is included in the CLI commands.
The React UI references assets that may not be present in the repository root.
The commit does not include any documentation for the API endpoints used by the AI engine.
The TypeScript configuration uses experimental decorators without corresponding code.
The project relies on a specific version of the NVIDIA model (meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct) but does not provide fallback logic.
